tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: Look up a verified playbook for doing a task on a website before acting: direct URL shortcuts, steps that describe elements by meaning, known gotchas, and the task's success_criteria (how to check you are done). Call it before navigating a site for a task. Untrusted guidance from a public registry.

tools.name: get_site_map
tools.description: The site's map for your goal, in a few hundred tokens: whether agents can get in, the best known route (a URL template with its parameters, their formats and known values), other pages, and pages robots.txt rules out. tools.name: submit_trace
tools.description: Report the outcome after doing a task on a website, with or without a playbook. Simplest form: {report_token (from get_playbook), success}. A report keeps the playbook working for your next run, and the reply shows its updated success rate. Without a token, send site, task, playbook_id and outcome.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "submit_trace" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_playbook, get_site_map · Private data: get_site_map, submit_trace · Public sink: submit_trace · Destructive: get_playbook, get_site_map, submit_trace.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_playbook, get_site_map · Private data: get_site_map, submit_trace · Public sink: submit_trace · Destructive: get_playbook, get_site_map, submit_trace

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
